analysis.investment_thesis: Choice International trades at P/E 77x and P/S 16x for a small capital markets broker-NBFC with only 921 Cr revenue — this is pure speculation, not investing. OCF has been negative in 4 of the last 5 years and FCF collapsed to -451 Cr in 2025; the company is burning cash while the stock market assigns a 16,163 Cr market cap.
key_strengths: Strong revenue and profit growth acceleration — revenue CAGR 19.4%, profit CAGR 51% over 9 years
ROE of 19.6% and ROCE of 20% show genuine operating efficiency
Diversified financial services model across broking, NBFC, wealth management, and insurance distribution
key_risks: Capital markets broking is highly cyclical — volumes and revenues will fall sharply in a bear market
Promoter holding at 53.66% is below my 55% threshold and is uncomfortably low for a financial services firm
Finance costs nearly tripled in 3 years (15 Cr to 66 Cr), reflecting rising debt to fund growth
red_flags: P/E of 77x is an extreme valuation — I would never pay this for any business, let alone a cyclical one
OCF negative in 4/5 years; FCF -451 Cr in 2025 — the business consumes more cash than it generates
Financing CF +449 Cr in 2025 means growth is funded entirely by external capital, not internal cash
P/S of 16x for a financial services company with 921 Cr revenue is disconnected from reality
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is exactly the kind of 'glamour growth stock' I have spent my career avoiding. The business may well be growing fast, but when you pay 77 times earnings for a company that generates negative operating cash flows, you are buying a story, not a business. Capital markets firms are inherently volatile — their revenues can halve in a bad year — and at this valuation there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
